en: Using an inclined plane like a wooden ramp reduces the force needed to push a heavy wheelchair, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with wet floors, preventing dangerous slips and falls during the rainy season.
Storing heavy canned goods on lower shelves uses gravity safely, preventing them from falling and causing head injuries.
Strong neodymium magnets can erase data on credit cards and interfere with pacemakers, so keep them stored safely away.
Water conducts electricity, so you must never touch plugged-in appliances with wet hands to avoid severe electric shocks.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light, preventing long-term damage to your eyes during sunny days.
Listening to loud music through earphones for hours damages hair cells in the inner ear, causing permanent hearing loss.
Using a dry wooden spoon as a thermal insulator prevents heat from burning your hands when stirring hot soup.
Eating a banana provides chemical energy that your body converts into mechanical energy for playing and moving muscles.
A bottle opener acts as a second-class lever, multiplying your hand force to safely pop off tight metal caps.
Plugging too many appliances into one extension cord causes overheating, which can melt the wires and start a house fire.
Rubbing your hands together quickly converts mechanical energy into thermal energy through friction, warming your skin during cold weather.
